title: Quota enforcement reliability: degrader mode, multi-region replication, and fair burst handling
creator: Ava Thompson
description:
Problem: Our global quota enforcement relies on a central limiter service and an eventual-consistent global state. When the limiter experiences outages or cross-region connectivity drops, we observe large-scale SLO violations (quota overshoots and customer-facing 429/503 spikes), unfair burst behavior where noisy tenants consume disproportionate capacity, and degraded visibility in the Console.

Goal: Design and ship a robust quota enforcement architecture that preserves SLOs during partial failures and high-burst scenarios. Key capabilities: local degrader/fallback mode during limiter outages, bounded and fair burst semantics per tenant, multi-region replication/lease model for global quotas, circuit breaker integration to avoid cascading failures, predictable load shedding by priority, and observability + runbook for incident response.

Success criteria / Acceptance criteria:
- During simulated limiter outage (Partition-A), <= 1% additional SLO errors across canary customers; no large capacity steal by a single tenant.
- Burst fairness: top-10 noisy tenants must not consume > 3x the median per-tenant throughput over a 1-minute window in stable mode.
- Degrader mode should re-enable within 2s of detecting limiter health failure and fallback to local best-effort limits with eventual reconciliation.
- Rolling canary deployment to 5% traffic shows no > 5% latency regressions at p99.

Proposed design (high-level):
1) Local-First Token Buckets + Soft Global Quotas:
   - Each serving region maintains local token buckets for short-term bursts (burst window = 3s, refill rate = global_rate/regions).
   - Global quotas enforced via a lease-backed aggregator (periodic heartbeat to a global coordinator). If leases fail, regions flip to Degrader Mode where local buckets enforce conservative soft caps.

2) Degrader Mode Behavior:
   - Enter when limiter healthcheck fails (3 consecutive failed RPCs or >50ms tail increases + error rate).
   - Switch to best-effort local enforcement using conservative quotas derived from last-good global snapshot + scaled guardrail (-20%).
   - Emit telemetry flag (limit_mode=degrader, limiter_version=last_seen) so Console and billing logic know limits are tentative.

3) Fairness and Burst Management:
   - Weighted Deficit Round Robin (WDRR) across tenant queues to ensure proportional fairness during bursts. Weights derived from customer tier + historical baseline throughput.
   - Short-term per-tenant burst buckets with deny-backpressure when abuse detected (exponential backoff per offending tenant).

4) Circuit Breaker & Load Shedding Integration:
   - Circuit breaker sits between router and limiter client; if limiter latency/error rate passes threshold, open circuit, route traffic to degrader.
   - Load shedding policy layered by priority: free-tier -> best-effort shedding first, then standard, then enterprise. Shedding uses gradual percentage steps (10% -> 25% -> 50%) and falls back to 429s with explanatory headers.

5) State persistence & reconciliation:
   - Periodic snapshots of local bucket state to a replicated Redis cluster (configurable ttl). On limiter recovery, perform reconciliation: replay consumed tokens to coordinator and correct global counters using vector-clock-ish reconciliation window (<= 30s).

6) Observability & Alerting:
   - New metrics: limiter.rpc_latency_p99, limiter.rpc_errors, limit_mode{normal,degrader}, per_tenant_burst_consumption, fairness_violation_count.
   - Dashboards: Quota Enforcement Overview (global/regional), Degrader Incidents heatmap, Top-20 bursty tenants.
   - Alerts: pager if limit_mode=degrader in >1 region for >2m OR fairness_violation_count > 50 in 5m.

Design tradeoffs considered:
- Strong global consistency vs availability: We choose availability for short bursts (local buckets) and eventual consistency with reconciliation to avoid high latency on every request.
- Durable counters add cost and complexity; snapshots reduce write amplification but make exact accounting more complex on recovery.
- Fairness algorithms (WDRR) add CPU overhead under tight SLOs; we will micro-benchmark WDRR vs simple weighted-leaky-bucket in perf tests.

Security & Compliance notes: any persisted quota state must be encrypted at rest (KMS) and appear in audit logs. This triggers a security review (see metadata).

Implementation plan (milestones):
- Week 1: Prototype local degrader mode and health detectors (ENG-7832-A).
- Week 2: Implement WDRR fairness and per-tenant burst buckets, unit + integration tests (ENG-7832-B).
- Week 3: Reconciliation + snapshotting to Redis with KMS encryption (ENG-7832-C).
- Week 4: Staging chaos tests (network partitions + limiter OOM), metrics + dashboards, runbook draft (ENG-7832-D).
- Week 5: Canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% rollout with monitoring gates (ENG-7832-E).

Runbook highlights:
- Detection: limit_mode=degrader alert triggers paging.
- Immediate mitigation: disable non-critical background traffic via featureflag; apply temporary stricter per-tenant caps.
- Recovery: allow reconciliation to settle; if discrepancies > 1% of quota, trigger manual correction job.

- Perf microbench PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/10134
